notes: MTG defines the canonical nouns. Vox Mana defines the meaning beside them.
Consumers should render plain-language interpretation near specialized tags.
Use typal as the canonical tag; tribal remains an alias.

tags.canonical_definition: Using the graveyard as an active game zone or resource.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Treating loss as stored material rather than an ending.
tags.table_feel: Cards keep mattering after they leave the battlefield or hand.
tags.player_fantasy: Finding value in what others think is already spent.
typical_actions: cast or return cards from the graveyard
tags.new_player_note: This is not just having cards in the graveyard. It means your deck expects to use that zone.

tags.canonical_definition: Returning cards from the graveyard or replaying used resources.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making removal and sacrifice feel temporary.
tags.table_feel: Your best pieces keep coming back for another exchange.
tags.player_fantasy: Refusing to let a useful thing stay buried.
tags.new_player_note: Recursion is the broad pattern; reanimator is a narrower creature-to-battlefield version.

tags.canonical_definition: Putting creature cards from graveyards directly onto the battlefield.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning the graveyard into a shortcut for large threats.
tags.table_feel: Dead creatures become live pressure again, often ahead of schedule.
tags.player_fantasy: Raising the best monster twice.
tags.new_player_note: Reanimator usually cares about creatures specifically and often cheats on mana costs.

tags.canonical_definition: Putting cards from your own library into your graveyard on purpose.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Digging downward to create future options.
tags.table_feel: Your graveyard fills quickly and starts acting like a second hand.
tags.player_fantasy: Burying seeds now so the later game can bloom.
tags.new_player_note: Self-mill is not the same as trying to deck an opponent. It fuels your own graveyard plan.

tags.canonical_definition: Sacrificing your own permanents for value, protection, or triggers.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Spending pieces before opponents can define their worth.
tags.table_feel: Small permanents turn into cards, mana, damage, or inevitability.
tags.player_fantasy: Commanding a machine where every part has a final use.
tags.new_player_note: Sacrifice decks need both things to sacrifice and reasons to sacrifice them.

tags.canonical_definition: Winning through creatures dying, sacrifice loops, and drain or value payoffs.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making every exchange costly for the whole table.
tags.table_feel: Opponents lose ground whenever your own pieces die.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning a board of expendable bodies into an elegant debt engine.
tags.new_player_note: The name is an MTG archetype term. It usually means sacrifice plus death-trigger payoffs.

tags.canonical_definition: Creating token permanents, especially creature tokens, as resources or threats.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Building presence through many bodies or temporary objects.
tags.table_feel: Your battlefield keeps producing extra material.
tags.player_fantasy: Leading an army or workshop instead of relying on one card.
typical_actions: use tokens as attackers or fodder
tags.new_player_note: Tokens can be attackers, blockers, sacrifice fuel, artifact resources, or combo pieces.

tags.canonical_definition: Winning by building many creatures and scaling their combined pressure.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Overwhelming the table through scale and momentum.
tags.table_feel: Combat math becomes harder every turn your board survives.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning with the host, not the lone champion.
tags.new_player_note: Go-wide is about board width as the pressure engine, not merely owning several creatures.

tags.canonical_definition: Rewarding the casting of instants and sorceries, often in chains.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making the stack itself feel like the battlefield.
tags.table_feel: Small spells build velocity until a payoff turn arrives.
tags.player_fantasy: Conducting a sequence where each spell sharpens the next.
tags.new_player_note: Spellslinger usually needs cheap spells, payoffs, and protection for the big turn.

tags.canonical_definition: Casting many spells in one turn, sometimes using the Storm keyword.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning momentum into a single overwhelming crescendo.
tags.table_feel: One turn becomes a long stack of rituals, draw, copies, and payoffs.
tags.player_fantasy: Solving the turn like a spellcraft puzzle under pressure.
tags.new_player_note: Storm can be powerful and complex. In Commander it often asks the table to follow a long turn.

tags.canonical_definition: Copying instants, sorceries, or other spells for extra effects.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making one clever spell echo into many outcomes.
tags.table_feel: A single spell can become removal, value, and surprise at once.
tags.player_fantasy: Amplifying precision into spectacle.
tags.new_player_note: Copying a spell usually copies its effect, not the physical card.

tags.canonical_definition: Gaining life as protection, fuel, or a payoff trigger.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning endurance into a resource engine.
tags.table_feel: Your life total moves upward and starts unlocking payoffs.
tags.player_fantasy: Surviving long enough for devotion, debt, or growth to take over.
tags.new_player_note: Lifegain is strongest when it does something besides only raising your life total.

tags.canonical_definition: Making opponents lose life while you gain life or value.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Converting every exchange into a quiet toll.
tags.table_feel: The table's life totals shrink while yours stays buffered.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning by making the room pay for every step.
tags.new_player_note: Drain is not combat damage. It often bypasses blockers and affects every opponent.

tags.canonical_definition: Using counters on permanents or players as a scaling resource.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting small increments become visible transformation.
tags.table_feel: Pieces grow, remember previous turns, and become harder to ignore.
tags.player_fantasy: Improving the same thing until it changes category.
tags.new_player_note: Counters can mean many things. This tag usually means permanent-based counters, especially +1/+1 counters.

tags.canonical_definition: Choosing permanents or players with counters and giving each another counter of a kind already there.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting every mark on the table deepen at once.
tags.table_feel: Small counters compound across many objects.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning a single experiment into system-wide growth.
tags.new_player_note: Proliferate does not create a new counter type. It adds to counters that already exist.

tags.canonical_definition: Using artifacts as threats, engines, mana, or synergy pieces.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Building power out of crafted objects and repeatable tools.
tags.table_feel: The board fills with engines, trinkets, and modular resources.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning through invention, relics, or machinery.
typical_actions: use artifacts for mana or sacrifice
tags.new_player_note: Artifacts can be creatures, equipment, mana rocks, tokens, or combo pieces.

tags.canonical_definition: Creating Treasure artifact tokens for temporary mana or artifact synergies.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Banking opportunity until the decisive turn.
tags.table_feel: Unused objects become burst mana or sacrifice fuel later.
tags.player_fantasy: Hoarding resources and spending them explosively.
tags.new_player_note: Treasure is temporary mana, but it also counts as artifacts for many effects.

tags.canonical_definition: Creating Clue artifact tokens that can be sacrificed to draw cards.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning investigation into delayed knowledge.
tags.table_feel: You bank small artifacts that become cards when time allows.
tags.player_fantasy: Following evidence until it becomes advantage.
tags.new_player_note: Clues cost mana to cash in, so they reward patience and spare mana.

tags.canonical_definition: Creating Food artifact tokens for life gain, sacrifice, or synergy.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Storing survival in small, expendable offerings.
tags.table_feel: Your board carries backup life and artifact fuel.
tags.player_fantasy: Feeding engines, creatures, or the table itself.
tags.new_player_note: Food is often more useful when the deck has payoffs beyond gaining life.

tags.canonical_definition: Using Equipment artifacts to enhance creatures repeatedly.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making one body carry crafted identity and pressure.
tags.table_feel: One creature becomes a must-answer threat through attached tools.
tags.player_fantasy: Forging a champion piece by piece.
tags.new_player_note: Equipment stays on the battlefield when the creature dies, so it can be reused.

tags.canonical_definition: Using enchantments as persistent rules, engines, or creature enhancements.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Writing ongoing conditions into the game.
tags.table_feel: The battlefield gains durable rules that shape every turn.
tags.player_fantasy: Binding the table with vows, laws, curses, or blessings.
tags.new_player_note: Enchantments often sit in play and keep changing how the game works.

tags.canonical_definition: Drawing cards or gaining value whenever enchantments are cast or enter.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting every oath, curse, or blessing replace itself.
tags.table_feel: Your enchantments become both board presence and card flow.
tags.player_fantasy: Weaving a spellwork engine that rewards each new binding.
tags.new_player_note: Enchantress decks need enough enchantments to keep their engines running.

tags.canonical_definition: Getting access to more mana than normal for your turn count.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Opening bigger doors earlier than the table expects.
tags.table_feel: You move from setup into large plays ahead of schedule.
tags.player_fantasy: Growing the ritual circle until bigger spells become natural.
tags.new_player_note: Ramp is strongest when you have meaningful expensive plays to ramp into.

tags.canonical_definition: Producing very large amounts of mana for oversized plays.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning resource scale into inevitability.
tags.table_feel: Your turns ask questions that normal mana cannot answer cleanly.
tags.player_fantasy: Casting the kind of spell that changes the room.
typical_actions: scale mana with lands or creatures
tags.new_player_note: Big mana is not just ramp. It is ramp aimed at very large payoffs.

tags.canonical_definition: Triggering effects when lands enter the battlefield under your control.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making ordinary development feel alive and responsive.
tags.table_feel: Every land drop becomes pressure, value, or growth.
tags.player_fantasy: Letting the world itself answer your plan.
tags.new_player_note: Landfall decks care about making land drops repeatedly, sometimes more than casting spells.

tags.canonical_definition: Using lands as central resources beyond normal mana production.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Treating the ground as an engine, not scenery.
tags.table_feel: Lands move, return, trigger, sacrifice, and become threats.
tags.player_fantasy: Commanding the landscape as part of the spell.
tags.new_player_note: This is broader than Landfall and can include land recursion, utility lands, and land creatures.

tags.canonical_definition: Winning or gaining value through attacks, blocks, and combat damage.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Resolving identity through visible pressure.
tags.table_feel: Board positioning and attack choices decide the game.
tags.player_fantasy: Making creatures matter in the red zone.
tags.new_player_note: Combat decks still need card advantage and protection; attacking alone is rarely enough.

tags.canonical_definition: Creating additional combat phases to attack more than once.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Refusing to let one decisive assault be enough.
tags.table_feel: One attack step becomes several and life totals collapse quickly.
tags.player_fantasy: Leading a charge that keeps finding another opening.
tags.new_player_note: Extra combat is strongest with creatures that attack well or trigger when they attack.

tags.canonical_definition: Building one creature, often a commander, into a lethal protected threat.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Condensing the whole plan into a single champion.
tags.table_feel: One creature demands immediate answers every turn.
tags.player_fantasy: Making one hero carry the story.
tags.new_player_note: Voltron decks need protection because losing the main creature can cost a lot of tempo.

tags.canonical_definition: Exiling permanents and returning them to reuse enter-the-battlefield effects or dodge removal.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting a permanent step out of the story and re-enter changed.
tags.table_feel: ETB effects repeat and removal becomes less reliable.
tags.player_fantasy: Mastering timing by making objects vanish at the exact moment.
tags.new_player_note: Blink usually returns your own cards and often resets Auras, counters, or choices.

tags.canonical_definition: Using effects that trigger when permanents enter the battlefield.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making arrival itself a source of value.
tags.table_feel: Every permanent can bring a spell-like effect with it.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning creatures into repeated tools and messengers.
tags.new_player_note: ETB is shorthand for 'enters the battlefield.'

tags.canonical_definition: Putting cards from libraries into graveyards, often to win by emptying an opponent's library.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Attacking the future draws before they can happen.
tags.table_feel: Libraries shrink and graveyards fill under pressure.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning by erasing possibilities.
tags.new_player_note: Mill can target yourself or opponents. This tag usually means using mill as pressure or a win condition.

tags.canonical_definition: Forcing players to discard cards or gaining value from discarded cards.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Controlling what choices survive to the table.
tags.table_feel: Hands shrink and hidden plans become fragile.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning before threats can even be cast.
typical_actions: discard your own cards for value
tags.new_player_note: Discard can be frustrating in casual games; use it with a clear win plan.

tags.canonical_definition: Making players discard or shuffle hands and draw new cards.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Resetting the room's possibilities at your chosen tempo.
tags.table_feel: Everyone's hand changes, but your deck is built to profit most.
tags.player_fantasy: Spinning fate and being ready for where it lands.
tags.new_player_note: Wheels refill opponents too, so the payoff needs to justify the reset.

tags.canonical_definition: Drawing extra cards or gaining sustained access to more options.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Keeping the hand alive with fresh possibility.
tags.table_feel: You have more choices and recover faster from trades.
tags.player_fantasy: Always finding the next tool.
tags.new_player_note: Draw is a support engine for many decks, not always the main identity.

tags.canonical_definition: Using spells or abilities to deal direct damage to creatures, players, or any target.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Solving problems with immediate heat.
tags.table_feel: Life totals and creatures are pressured without needing combat.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning a spell into a clean strike.
tags.new_player_note: Commander life totals are high, so burn often needs scaling or repeated triggers.

tags.canonical_definition: Damaging or draining all opponents, often repeatedly, for normal game actions.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making the table pay rent for existing.
tags.table_feel: Every turn cycle bleeds life totals across the table.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning the room into a pressure chamber.
tags.new_player_note: Group slug affects everyone and can make you a target quickly.

tags.canonical_definition: Giving resources to multiple players, often to shape politics or chaos.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Using generosity as influence.
tags.table_feel: Everyone gets extra cards, mana, or choices, but alliances shift around you.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the host who decides what abundance costs.
tags.new_player_note: Group hug needs a win condition; helping everyone can help opponents win first.

tags.canonical_definition: Combining specific cards or effects to create an overwhelming or repeating outcome.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Finding the hidden lock where separate pieces become one machine.
tags.table_feel: The game can pivot suddenly when the pieces align.
tags.player_fantasy: Solving the deck like an intricate mechanism.
tags.new_player_note: Combo can be finite or infinite. Tell your table what power level you are aiming for.

tags.canonical_definition: Using opponents' cards, permanents, libraries, or graveyards as resources.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning enemy material into your own leverage.
tags.table_feel: Opponents must play around their best cards being used against them.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning with what the table brought to stop you.
tags.new_player_note: Theft can create memory and ownership complexity in paper games.

tags.canonical_definition: Using exile as removal, protection, storage, or a cast-from-exile resource.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Putting something outside the normal cycle of return.
tags.table_feel: Some cards leave the usual graveyard economy entirely.
tags.player_fantasy: Sealing threats beyond ordinary recovery.
tags.new_player_note: Exile is usually harder to recover from than the graveyard, but some decks use exile as a resource.

tags.canonical_definition: Building around a shared creature type and cards that reward that type.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Finding identity through kinship and repeated symbols.
tags.table_feel: Creatures become stronger because they belong to the same lineage or role.
tags.player_fantasy: Leading a people, pack, crew, or order.
typical_actions: play many creatures of that type
tags.new_player_note: Typal is the current preferred term. Tribal remains a legacy search synonym.

tags.canonical_definition: A proactive strategy that pressures opponents early through damage or threats.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Forcing the table to answer before comfort becomes a plan.
tags.table_feel: Life totals matter early and opponents are put on the back foot.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the first blade drawn.
tags.new_player_note: Aggro in Commander needs staying power because there are multiple opponents.

tags.canonical_definition: A reactive strategy that answers threats and wins after stabilizing.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Choosing what is allowed to matter.
tags.table_feel: The table must commit into open mana, sweepers, or precise removal.
tags.player_fantasy: Holding the final verdict until the right moment.
tags.new_player_note: Control is not answering everything. It is answering what matters most.

tags.canonical_definition: Gaining advantage by making opponents spend more time and mana than you do.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Winning by making every turn arrive slightly too late for opponents.
tags.table_feel: Threats bounce, tap, or get delayed while your pressure continues.
tags.player_fantasy: Dancing one step ahead of the table.
tags.new_player_note: Tempo is about time and pressure, not just speed.

tags.canonical_definition: A flexible strategy built on efficient threats, answers, and repeatable value.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Winning by making each exchange leave you slightly ahead.
tags.table_feel: Your deck adapts to the table and keeps trading profitably.
tags.player_fantasy: Having the right tool without needing a fragile plan.
tags.new_player_note: Midrange often feels fair, but it still needs a way to end the game.

tags.canonical_definition: A strategy centered on assembling a specific winning interaction.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Building toward the moment where the hidden pattern locks into place.
tags.table_feel: The game may look stable until one protected turn ends it.
tags.player_fantasy: Solving the puzzle before the table can break it.
tags.new_player_note: Combo power varies widely. Talk with the table about expectations.

tags.canonical_definition: Restricting resources, actions, or timing so opponents cannot execute normal plans.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Constraining the table until only your path remains workable.
tags.table_feel: Spells cost more, permanents stay tapped, and choices narrow.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning by setting the rules of scarcity.
tags.new_player_note: Stax can create slow games. Use it knowingly and communicate power level.

tags.canonical_definition: Using deals, incentives, goad, votes, or threat assessment to shape decisions.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Treating alliances and attention as resources.
tags.table_feel: The best play may be social, not just mechanical.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning the room before winning the game.
tags.new_player_note: Politics works best when deals are clear and the deck can still win on cards.

tags.canonical_definition: Introducing random, unpredictable, or table-wide effects that disrupt normal planning.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Breaking certainty so instinct and improvisation matter.
tags.table_feel: Everyone has to adapt to changing conditions.
tags.player_fantasy: Becoming the storm the table must navigate.
tags.new_player_note: Chaos is memorable but can reduce agency if overused.

tags.canonical_definition: Discouraging attacks through taxes, prevention, blockers, or protective enchantments.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Building a sanctuary that makes aggression inefficient.
tags.table_feel: Opponents can attack elsewhere more easily than they can attack you.
tags.player_fantasy: Surviving behind wards until the real plan awakens.
tags.new_player_note: Pillow fort still needs a win condition; safety alone rarely ends a Commander game.

tags.canonical_definition: Small creatures that restrict opponents' actions while applying pressure.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Putting rules on legs and making them attack.
tags.table_feel: Every small creature carries an annoying clause opponents must answer.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning through disciplined interference.
tags.new_player_note: Hatebears are usually fragile, so sequencing and protection matter.

tags.canonical_definition: Using tutors or flexible cards to find specialized answers or threats.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Keeping a hidden drawer for whatever the table asks.
tags.table_feel: Your deck can pivot into narrow answers at the right time.
tags.player_fantasy: Always knowing which instrument to pull from the case.
tags.new_player_note: Toolbox decks reward format knowledge and can slow down if every turn involves a search.

tags.canonical_definition: Playing individually strong cards in a color identity rather than deep synergy.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Trusting raw card quality and flexible power.
tags.table_feel: Every draw is broadly useful, even without a named engine.
tags.player_fantasy: Carrying a deck of proven answers and threats.
tags.new_player_note: Goodstuff is easy to start but can feel unfocused without a theme or finish.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme centered on death, dying, and the meaning of endings.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Seeing endings as material, memory, or cost.
tags.table_feel: Death triggers and graveyard resources shape the story.
tags.player_fantasy: Finding power where others see finality.
tags.new_player_note: Death themes are often mechanical graveyard or sacrifice themes, but the fantasy can be broader.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of rot, corrosion, and transformation through breakdown.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting old forms become food for the next form.
tags.table_feel: Resources are consumed, reduced, and remade.
tags.player_fantasy: Commanding the composting edge of power.
tags.new_player_note: Decay is not only evil. Vox Mana often reads it as transformation through breakdown.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of learning, information, proof, or hidden truth.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power through understanding what others miss.
tags.table_feel: Cards, clues, and timing reveal the winning line.
tags.player_fantasy: Knowing the shape of the game before it arrives.
tags.new_player_note: Knowledge can look like card draw, clues, scrying, or careful control.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of striving for power, status, mastery, or ascent.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Wanting more and being willing to structure a plan around it.
tags.table_feel: Resources become leverage toward a larger claim.
tags.player_fantasy: Rising because the table underestimated your appetite.
tags.new_player_note: Ambition is a tone, not a morality label. It can be noble, ruthless, or both.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of structure, discipline, systems, and clear constraints.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Believing the table is safer or stronger when rules have weight.
tags.table_feel: The game narrows into defined lanes and enforceable choices.
tags.player_fantasy: Writing the procedure everyone must respect.
tags.new_player_note: Order can protect, restrict, or dominate depending on deck expression.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of defiance against authority, control, or imposed limits.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Breaking the shape that was handed to you.
tags.table_feel: Rules and expectations get challenged directly.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the spark that refuses the cage.
tags.new_player_note: Rebellion can be aggressive, chaotic, or protective depending on the deck.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of creating devices, engines, prototypes, or new methods.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Solving the table by building a better instrument.
tags.table_feel: Artifacts, copies, and engines make the deck feel constructed in motion.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the mind behind the machine.
tags.new_player_note: Invention often pairs with artifacts, spellslinger, or combo patterns.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of devotion, worship, vows, blessing, or spiritual conviction.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power grounded in belief made visible.
tags.table_feel: Enchantments, life, protection, or sacrifice carry ritual weight.
tags.player_fantasy: Making conviction into a battlefield force.
tags.new_player_note: Faith can be comforting, authoritarian, sacrificial, or restorative depending on context.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of fear, monsters, nightmares, or unsettling transformation.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making uncertainty and dread into pressure.
tags.table_feel: The game feels dangerous even before the threat is fully visible.
tags.player_fantasy: Becoming the thing at the edge of the room.
tags.new_player_note: Horror is a fantasy tone and can appear in many mechanics.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of vast, alien, celestial, or reality-scale forces.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Feeling small in front of a power too large to domesticate.
tags.table_feel: Scale and inevitability matter more than ordinary table concerns.
tags.player_fantasy: Calling on something older or stranger than the game state.
tags.new_player_note: Cosmic does not always mean colorless, but it often feels vast or alien.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of wilderness, ecosystems, beasts, and natural cycles.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power as something grown, hunted, rooted, or restored.
tags.table_feel: Lands, creatures, and growth drive the game forward.
tags.player_fantasy: Letting the world itself join your side.
tags.new_player_note: Nature can be peaceful, predatory, restorative, or furious.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of becoming larger, better, more numerous, or more developed over time.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Trusting accumulation and adaptation to transform the board.
tags.table_feel: Small advantages compound until the table must answer them.
tags.player_fantasy: Watching the plan become more alive each turn.
tags.new_player_note: Growth can mean bigger creatures, more resources, or a board that improves over time.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of gut response, predation, survival, or embodied action.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Knowing through motion rather than argument.
tags.table_feel: The deck favors direct lines and creature pressure.
tags.player_fantasy: Trusting the hunt before the committee arrives.
tags.new_player_note: Instinct can be smart and adaptive; it is not the same as random play.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of fury, explosive force, revenge, or emotional rupture.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Turning pain or refusal into immediate force.
tags.table_feel: Damage, attacks, and risky swings arrive fast.
tags.player_fantasy: Breaking the room open because waiting would be a lie.
tags.new_player_note: Rage can express justice, chaos, survival, or destruction.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of escape, autonomy, open possibility, or refusal of limits.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Keeping movement possible when the table tries to close around you.
tags.table_feel: The deck resists locks, breaks parity, or acts unpredictably.
tags.player_fantasy: Refusing to ask permission to become yourself.
tags.new_player_note: Freedom can be protective or disruptive depending on how it is expressed.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of laws, courts, verdicts, contracts, or enforceable obligation.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making abstract rules bite the table.
tags.table_feel: Choices have consequences and violations are punished.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the judge, not the petitioner.
tags.new_player_note: Law can appear as protection, control, taxation, or punishment.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of hidden information, concealment, spies, or withheld motives.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Keeping power unspoken until timing makes it decisive.
tags.table_feel: Opponents are unsure what matters until it is too late.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning from behind the curtain.
tags.new_player_note: Secrecy often pairs with control, theft, discard, or evasive creatures.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of remembrance, history, records, legacy, or the past returning.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting what happened before remain active in the present.
tags.table_feel: Graveyards, artifacts, and old decisions keep mattering.
tags.player_fantasy: Calling the past as witness and weapon.
tags.new_player_note: Memory can be literal graveyard play or lore-facing artifact/history play.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of collapse, broken places, destroyed systems, or aftermath.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Finding meaning in what remains after the structure fails.
tags.table_feel: Destruction and recovery shape the board state.
tags.player_fantasy: Standing in the rubble with a plan.
tags.new_player_note: Ruin is not only destruction; it can also be survival after destruction.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of healing, rebuilding, returning, or making whole.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Repairing without pretending nothing was lost.
tags.table_feel: Damaged boards recover and useful pieces return.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the hand that rebuilds after the blow.
tags.new_player_note: Restoration can be gentle, stubborn, or strategic.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of discovery, questions, experiments, or the desire to know more.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Following the unknown because it calls louder than certainty.
tags.table_feel: The deck draws, investigates, experiments, or rewards strange lines.
tags.player_fantasy: Opening one more door just to see what answers.
tags.new_player_note: Curiosity can be careful scholarship or volatile experimentation.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of steering choices, controlling resources, or exploiting incentives.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Winning by arranging what others think they chose freely.
tags.table_feel: The table's decisions bend around your hidden structure.
tags.player_fantasy: Pulling the string that everyone else mistook for chance.
tags.new_player_note: Manipulation can be political, mechanical, or villainous in tone.

tags.canonical_definition: A theme of shared strength, kinship, protection, or collective purpose.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that becomes real because it is held together.
tags.table_feel: Many pieces support each other and scale through belonging.
tags.player_fantasy: Leading a table presence that feels like a people, not a pile.
tags.new_player_note: Community can be peaceful, militant, political, or sacrificial.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of waiting, restraint, and careful timing.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that trusts the later turn.
tags.table_feel: The deck waits for the exact opening before committing.
tags.player_fantasy: Letting the table move first because you know what matters.
tags.new_player_note: Patient does not mean passive. It means timing matters.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone that suggests the ending is already approaching.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: A slow pressure that becomes harder to deny each turn.
tags.table_feel: Opponents feel the game closing even before the final move.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the clock the table noticed too late.
tags.new_player_note: Inevitability usually comes from repeatable advantage, not a single big card.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of appetite, consumption, and need.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that must feed to keep becoming.
tags.table_feel: Resources are eaten, sacrificed, drained, or converted.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the engine that is never full.
tags.new_player_note: Hungry is a tone and can appear in sacrifice, graveyard, or creature-heavy decks.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of honor, virtue, duty, or elevated purpose.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that wants its victory to mean something clean.
tags.table_feel: Protection, combat, and sacrifice carry a heroic charge.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning without feeling small inside the win.
tags.new_player_note: Noble is about tone, not power level.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of efficiency without softness or hesitation.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Doing what wins and letting sentiment arrive later, if at all.
tags.table_feel: The deck cuts resources, drains life, and uses pieces hard.
tags.player_fantasy: Choosing the cleanest cruel line.
tags.new_player_note: Ruthless is not automatically malicious, but it often feels sharp at the table.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of inquiry, wonder, and pursuit of answers.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Letting questions pull the deck forward.
tags.table_feel: The deck draws, investigates, tests, and pivots.
tags.player_fantasy: Opening the next sealed page.
tags.new_player_note: Curious can be gentle exploration or dangerous experimentation.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of age, deep time, old powers, or inherited weight.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power with roots older than the current conflict.
tags.table_feel: The deck feels slow, deep, and hard to fully remove.
tags.player_fantasy: Calling on something that remembers before anyone else arrived.
tags.new_player_note: Ancient can appear in artifacts, graveyards, lands, or cosmic threats.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of holiness, ritual, blessing, or protected meaning.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Treating the game plan as something vowed, not merely chosen.
tags.table_feel: Protection, life, enchantments, and devotion feel ritualized.
tags.player_fantasy: Keeping a flame that must not go out.
tags.new_player_note: Sacred can be benevolent, strict, or frightening depending on context.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of quiet unease, haunting, or uncanny presence.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Pressure that arrives as a whisper before it becomes a threat.
tags.table_feel: The board feels watched, haunted, or not fully knowable.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the silence opponents keep misreading.
tags.new_player_note: Eerie is a flavor tone and can sit beside many mechanics.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of disorder, volatility, and unstable outcomes.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Breaking the expected shape so new outcomes can happen.
tags.table_feel: The table must improvise around sudden changes.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the event nobody could prepare for.
tags.new_player_note: Chaotic decks are most fun when they still let players make meaningful decisions.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of training, precision, restraint, and exact execution.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that wins by refusing sloppy motion.
tags.table_feel: Every card seems to have a job and timing window.
tags.player_fantasy: Executing the clean line under pressure.
tags.new_player_note: Disciplined can belong to control, combat, stax, or any precise engine.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of shared effort, belonging, or collective identity.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power felt through the group rather than the isolated self.
tags.table_feel: Many pieces matter because they support each other.
tags.player_fantasy: Winning as a chorus, conclave, crew, or swarm.
tags.new_player_note: Communal is not always gentle. A community deck can be militant or sacrificial.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of grief, sacrifice, loss, or hard cost.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that remembers what it paid.
tags.table_feel: Deaths and losses feel meaningful rather than incidental.
tags.player_fantasy: Turning sorrow into a reason the game cannot ignore.
tags.new_player_note: Tragic tone can be beautiful, grim, or resilient.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of refusal, resistance, and standing against pressure.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that says no by continuing to exist.
tags.table_feel: The deck resists control, rebuilds, or attacks through opposition.
tags.player_fantasy: Standing back up where the table expected obedience.
tags.new_player_note: Defiance can be aggressive or defensive depending on the shell.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of trial, invention, prototype, and uncertain result.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Learning through motion, even when the motion sparks.
tags.table_feel: The deck tries strange lines and rewards flexible sequencing.
tags.player_fantasy: Building the device while it is already running.
tags.new_player_note: Experimental does not always mean random. It often means exploratory and iterative.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of hunting, prey, teeth, and pressure from above or below.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Power that watches for weakness and closes quickly.
tags.table_feel: Opponents feel targeted when shields drop.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the hunter, not the warning sign.
tags.new_player_note: Predatory is not only creature combat; it can also describe theft, discard, or pressure.

tags.canonical_definition: A tone of healing, renewal, recovery, and return.
tags.vox_mana_interpretation: Making repair into an active power.
tags.table_feel: The deck stabilizes, recovers, and makes damage less final.
tags.player_fantasy: Being the force that brings the board back from ruin.
tags.new_player_note: Restorative decks still need a way to pressure or finish the game.
